abstract: Under what conditions does externally supported energy transition planning produce locally owned and sustainable policy outcomes rather than short-lived plans, and what role do institutional gatekeeping, bureaucratic authority, and the sequencing of technical and political processes play in shaping those conditions? To unpack these questions, this paper comparatively analyses SEforALL's Energy Transition Investment Plan development in Ghana and Kenya, revealing striking divergences in processes and outcomes. Drawing on 22 semi-structured interviews and the theories of policy translation and political settlements, the analysis demonstrates that Ghana's experience was characterised by institutional bypass, limited domestic agency, and a significant reduction in the plan's operational priority following electoral change. Kenya's trajectory, conversely, featured institutional resistance that compelled collaborative engagement, resulting in sustainable policy embedding. The findings reveal that successful policy translation depends not merely on technical capacity but on power configuration, bureaucratic authority, and political settlements. This research advances understanding of energy transition politics whilst offering practical insights for international organisations and governments navigating the complex politics of translating global climate imperatives into national policies in developing countries.
title: Same intervention, different outcomes: The politics of energy transition planning in Ghana and Kenya

abstract: Subjected to the carbon neutrality goal, the carbon emissions trading scheme (CETS) has become an essential market-oriented tool for carbon emission reduction in high-emission sectors like the steel industry through the diffusion of low-carbon technologies. However, the heterogeneous responses to CETS across enterprises of different scales remain unclear, limiting the differentiated policy design. This study presents a tripartite evolutionary game model involving the government, large-scale steel enterprise (LSE), and small-scale steel enterprise (SSE) to investigate the low-carbon technology diffusion driven by CETS. By incorporating enterprise-scale heterogeneity like innovation capacity, financing constraints, risk preferences, and policy responsiveness, the model examines the evolutionary pathways of technology adoption under various policy and market conditions. The results show that the evolutionary trajectory of low-carbon technology adoption follows a staged framework but a non-sequential progression, encompassing four distinct scenarios including low-incentive, government-driven promotion, multi-stakeholder collaborative adoption, and industry self-regulation. Shifts between these scenarios are contingent on the interplay of carbon price, quota allocation and other policies considering scale heterogeneity. LSE is highly sensitive to carbon price, while SSE requires relatively light quota constraints combined with sufficiently high carbon price to overcome the barriers for technology diffusion. Furthermore, when collaboration costs fall below a certain threshold, it can effectively shorten the cycle of corporate strategic adjustments, prompting businesses to swiftly transition from partial adoption to comprehensive implementation of low-carbon technologies. This study provides the theoretical understanding of CETS-induced technology diffusion and targeted policy insights for advancing the low-carbon transformation of the steel industry.
title: Driving low-carbon technology diffusion in heterogeneous steel enterprises through carbon emissions trading: An evolutionary game analysis

abstract: We study the impact of Federal alcohol Prohibition in 1919 on workers in the alcohol industry and their families, using newly linked census records following spouses, sons, and daughters 1910-1940. Through 1930, affected men were less likely to work and worked in lower-skilled jobs when employed. By 1940, they were more likely to be employed, suggesting delayed retirement. Daughters of these workers were more likely to stay home, delay marriage, and work, even 20 years later. Sons were unaffected short-run. Those with sisters completed more schooling and earned more by 1940, suggesting daughters, not sons, served as the family’s safety net.
title: The Good Daughter?

abstract: We study political shocks as in-utero stressors, specifically the unexpected result of the 2016 U.S. presidential election. We investigate this shock using an innovative linkage: Colorado voter registrations and birth certificates, matched by sex, year, and name. While we do not find an effect on birth outcomes, we do find increased stress-related behaviors in pregnancy for Democrats and reduced prenatal care adequacy for Democrats and Independents, relative to Republicans. This adds new evidence on the effects of two-sided stressors, uses a novel data linkage, and expands the new economics area of politics as a determinant of health.
title: Political Stressors and Birth Outcomes

abstract: We introduce two families of inequality measures, $$G_p$$ G p and $$H_q$$ H q , that converge to the classical Gini coefficient as $$p,q\rightarrow \infty $$ p , q → ∞ . The tuning parameters $$p>1$$ p > 1 and $$q>0$$ q > 0 regulate the influence of disparities between observations. For each index we derive closed-form U -statistic plug-in estimators and establish strong consistency and asymptotic normality under mild moment conditions. A Monte Carlo study assesses finite-sample behavior across ( n , p , q ), and an empirical illustration with GDP per capita in the Americas shows how the tuning parameters influence the measure of inequality.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
title: Two tunable Gini-type measures with U-statistic estimation: theory, simulation, and an empirical application to GDP per capita in the Americas

abstract: This paper investigates how direct election regimes (à la presidential democracy) affect the gender composition of political leaders compared to indirect appointment regimes (à la parliamentary democracy). I study a 1993 reform that replaced mayoral appointment by councilors with direct election of mayors by popular vote in Italian municipalities. Exploiting the staggered adoption of the reform across municipalities between 1993 and 1997, I find that direct election raises the probability that a municipality is led by a woman by about 2.5 percentage points, from a pre-reform baseline of 3.5 percent to approximately 6 percent. The effect is stronger in municipalities with a greater pre-reform female representation in municipal councils and is driven by more educated officials replacing less-educated incumbents.
journal: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization
title: When women take all: Direct election and female leadership

abstract: We study Bayesian persuasion where the sender and receiver incur quadratic losses from deviating from their state-dependent bliss actions. Misalignment is captured by a flexible function mapping the sender’s bliss action to the receiver’s in each state of the world. We focus on the state-pooling structure of the optimal signal—that is, which subset of states is revealed by a signal realization—and show how it is shaped by the form of misalignment. We provide a method that yields a tight, prior-independent upper bound on the optimal pooling structure.
title: Bayesian p(h)ooling: Optimal pooling structure in quadratic Bayesian persuasion

abstract: In a widely cited article, Shiller (1997) found that the public dislikes inflation to a greater extent than economists—and dislikes inflation for different reasons. We fielded a contemporary version of Shiller’s survey to consider how economists’ and the public’s views on inflation have changed over time. We find that, in some respects, economists’ views on inflation more closely resemble those of the public in our survey than was originally reported by Shiller (1997). But important differences remain.
title: Reconsidering “Why do people dislike inflation?”

abstract: When the Federal Reserve raises interest rates, prices faced by younger households fall more than prices faced by older households. Using age-specific distributional consumer price indices together with high-frequency monetary policy shocks, we document a monotone age gradient in inflation responses, from households under 25 through households 75 and older. A simple decomposition combining BLS major-group CPI responses with age-specific CEX expenditure shares accounts for most of the gap between the youngest and oldest households. Transportation and medical care drive the result: younger households spend disproportionately on transportation (including motor fuel, vehicles, and auto insurance), whose prices respond strongly to monetary policy, while older households spend disproportionately on medical care, whose prices respond less.
title: Younger households’ inflation is more responsive to monetary policy

abstract: We examine time-of-day (TOD) effects on moral choice by comparing afternoon (DAY: 3pm-5pm) and nighttime (NIGHT: 3am-5am) decisions across three incentivized tasks. While the NIGHT treatment successfully induced sleepiness, we report no evidence that circadian suboptimality shifts decisions towards one’s default ethical tendencies. Rather, the NIGHT treatment increased dishonesty in a victimless Die-Roll task but not when dishonesty harms another participant (modified Coin-Flip task) or in consequential moral dilemmas affecting only others’ outcomes (Payoff-Trolley task). Exploratory response-times evidence is consistent with immoral choices resulting from deliberative processes. Overall, these results indicate that moral choice exhibits task-dependent stability during circadian fatigue.
title: Nighttime ethics: Do moral choices differ by time-of-day/night?

abstract: Would government intervention aimed at reducing socioeconomic inequalities lead to a healthier population and longer lives? We address this question using a structural life-cycle model with heterogeneous agents. The model is calibrated to U.S. survey and actuarial data, reproducing the age-at-death distribution, income inequality, medical expenditure patterns, the value of a statistical life, and the education–longevity gradient. We find that a universal basic income flattens the longevity gap across education levels but reduces overall longevity by weakening incentives for preventive care, a result that contrasts with recent statistical studies suggesting redistribution would increase population longevity. Instead, subsidies for preventive care raise average longevity but steepen the education–longevity gradient. In both cases, welfare effects remain uneven across education groups.
title: Income redistribution, preventive care, and longevity

abstract: We study how terrorist attacks targeting educational institutions affect private development aid through child sponsorship. Conceptually, terrorist events may increase sponsorship by signaling greater need or reduce it if affected communities are seen as less effective destinations to support. We combine global administrative data from Plan International on child sponsorship across 50 countries over the 2008-2018 period, aggregated at the Primary Sampling Unit (PSU) level, with geocoded terrorism events from the Global Terrorism Database. Our core specification focuses on attacks against educational institutions within 20 km of each PSU. We estimate the causal effect using a heterogeneity-robust difference-in-differences approach suited to staggered, non-absorbing treatments. We find that attacks on educational institutions reduce the share of sponsored children by about 3 percentage points, a 4 percent decline relative to the mean. Back-of-the-envelope calculations suggest this corresponds to funding losses of approximately US$615,000 across affected communities over the study period. Since sponsorship is geographically targeted, these losses fall on the specific communities, underscoring the need to buffer local development funding against security shocks.
title: Terrorism and Altruistic Giving: Evidence from Child Sponsorship

abstract: We show that gambling-style behaviour is important in politics: politicians ‛gamble for re-election‚ in the context of a political leader selection. We exploit unique access to leaked information on MPs' individual decisions in the 2021 leadership election of Germany's centre-right parties. MPs are more likely to vote for a riskier candidate when facing lower re-election chances. These results match the predictions derived from our model of rational risk-taking. Gambling for re-election shows that MPs trade off leaders' expected quality against their riskiness. It provides a new explanation for intra-party dissent, and rationalises why parties may choose low quality leaders.
title: Gambling for Re-election

abstract: Firms tend to compete more aggressively when facing financial distress. This intensified competition reduces profit margins, pushing them further into distress and adversely affecting their industry peers. To study such feedback and contagion effects, we incorporate strategic competition in a dynamic model with long‐term defaultable debt, exploring various peer interactions such as predation and price wars. The feedback effect represents a novel source of financial distress costs associated with leverage, which helps explain the negative profitability‐leverage relation across industries. Owing to the contagion effect, firms' optimal leverage is often excessively high from an industry perspective, undermining the industry's financial stability.
title: Feedback and Contagion through Distressed Competition

abstract: Leading up to Slovenia's entry into the EU, Slovenian exporters experienced large reductions in tariffs with their main trading partners, the EU member countries. We exploit variation in exports during this period to examine the role of exporting in the firms' recruiting practices. Data on all job vacancies and new hires in Slovenia during the 5 years preceding EU entry reveal that exporters created, on average, 30% of all vacancies and recruited 33% of new hires annually, despite comprising only 6% of all firms and 13% of all recruiting firms. Incumbent exporters were responsible for most recruiting. These differences in recruitment at the intensive and extensive margins had broader labour market implications. We find that labour markets with a larger presence of exporters had a more concentrated labour demand and, consistent with reduced coordination frictions, showed some signs of better matching of workers to job vacancies.
abstract_zh: 在斯洛文尼亚加入欧盟之前，斯洛文尼亚出口商与其主要贸易伙伴——欧盟成员国之间的关税大幅降低。我们利用这一时期出口的变化，考察出口在企业招聘实践中的作用。斯洛文尼亚加入欧盟前5年所有职位空缺和新雇员的数据显示，出口商平均创造了全部职位空缺的30%，每年招聘的新雇员占33%，尽管它们仅占所有企业的6%和所有招聘企业的13%。现有出口商承担了大部分招聘。这些在集约边际和广延边际上的招聘差异具有更广泛的劳动力市场影响。我们发现，出口商存在规模更大的劳动力市场具有更为集中的劳动力需求，并且与协调摩擦减少相一致，表现出一些工人与职位空缺更好匹配的迹象。
title: Recruitment by Exporters: Implications for Labour Demand Concentration and Labour Market Matching
title_zh: 出口商的招聘：对劳动力需求集中和劳动力市场匹配的影响

abstract: This paper studies how perceptions of own social class and local affluence shape preferences for redistribution. We conduct a survey experiment with 1293 respondents in Lima Metropolitana, randomly correcting beliefs either about respondents’ own socio-economic status (SES) under Peru’s official five-class classification, or about the share of affluent households in their district. Misperceptions are strongly asymmetric: about 70% of respondents overestimate their own SES and about 50% overestimate the local share of affluent households. The effects of information, however, are not uniform. The clearest evidence comes from respondents who substantially overestimate local affluence: correcting this belief increases support for redistribution. For own SES, effects are concentrated among respondents who overestimate their position by at least two classes (34% of the relevant sample); among respondents whose misperceptions are smaller, the evidence is weaker. Neither treatment shifts support for a wealth tax, and perceived fairness of the income distribution is largely unaffected. Using geocoded data, we further show that local SES and local affluence are positively associated with respondents’ perceptions, while local inequality itself is only weakly related to redistributive preferences in the control group. The results suggest that corrective information can affect redistributive attitudes when perceived-actual gaps are large, but that these effects depend on the type and magnitude of misperceptions.
abstract_zh: 本文研究个体对自身社会阶层与本地富裕程度的认知如何塑造再分配偏好。我们在利马都会区对1293名受访者开展了一项调查实验，随机校正受访者关于自身社会经济地位（SES）在秘鲁官方五阶层分类中所处位置的信念，或关于其所在地区富裕家庭占比的信念。认知偏差呈现显著的非对称性：约70%的受访者高估自身SES，约50%的受访者高估本地富裕家庭占比。然而，信息的影响并非一致。最清晰的证据来自大幅高估本地富裕程度的受访者：校正这一信念会提高其对再分配的支持。就自身SES而言，效应集中于将自身地位高估至少两个阶层的受访者（占相关样本的34%）；在认知偏差较小的受访者中，证据较弱。两种处理均未改变对财富税的支持，且收入分配的感知公平性基本未受影响。利用地理编码数据，我们进一步表明，本地SES与本地富裕程度同受访者的认知呈正相关，而本地不平等本身在控制组中与再分配偏好的关联较弱。结果表明，当感知与实际之间的差距较大时，校正性信息能够影响再分配态度，但这些效应取决于认知偏差的类型与幅度。
journal: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization
title: Perceptions of own social class and local affluence: Effects on preferences for redistribution
title_zh: 自身社会阶层认知与地方富裕程度：对再分配偏好的影响

abstract: In many countries outside the United States, students must choose an institution–major pair simultaneously, creating a trade‐off between institutional prestige and field of study. Using data from Taiwan's centralized admissions system, we study how applicants navigate this choice. We find that students strongly prioritize institutional ranking, with little heterogeneity across demographic groups and only a weak link between program choice and expected earnings. Counterfactual analysis shows that students forgo about 15% of their annual income by favoring institutions over earnings‐maximizing alternatives, suggesting that nonpecuniary factors—especially institutional reputation—play a central role in shaping college decisions.
abstract_zh: 在美国以外的许多国家，学生必须同时选择院校与专业组合，从而在院校声望与所学领域之间形成权衡。利用台湾集中招生系统的数据，我们研究了申请者如何应对这一选择。我们发现，学生强烈优先考虑院校排名，不同人口群体之间的异质性很小，且专业选择与预期收入之间仅存在微弱联系。反事实分析表明，学生因偏好院校而非收入最大化选项而放弃约15%的年收入，这表明非货币因素——尤其是院校声誉——在塑造大学决策中发挥核心作用。
china_relevance_reason: 研究使用台湾集中招生系统的数据，研究对象为中国台湾地区的学生升学选择，属于中国研究。
title: Institution or major? Understanding student preferences in college admissions
title_zh: 制度还是专业？理解大学招生中的学生偏好

abstract: Governments face increasing pressure to meet legally binding net-zero targets, requiring a rapid transition from internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles to electric vehicles (EVs). Designing effective incentive schemes is challenging because vehicle fleets adjust slowly, policy interventions are fiscally costly, and electrification erodes fuel-tax revenues. This paper develops a dynamic policy evaluation framework that combines cross-country evidence on EV adoption with long-run fleet dynamics under uncertainty. Using both the United Kingdom and France as case studies, we simulate optimal time paths of EV purchase incentives under alternative policy objectives, including terminal fleet targets, sales-based penalties, and fiscal revenue considerations. The results reveal three core findings. First, stock-based (terminal) penalties may delay intervention but strongly stabilize long-run fleet outcomes, while sales-based penalties induce earlier but less targeted action. Second, dependence on fuel-tax revenues creates a fiscal lock-in mechanism that weakens optimal electrification incentives. Third, the effectiveness of subsidy programs depends critically on consumer responsiveness to price incentives. Overall, the analysis shows that EV transition policy is best evaluated jointly with fiscal reform and long-run fleet dynamics. Well-timed and fiscally coherent intervention can substantially reduce emissions while limiting long-term budgetary risks.
abstract_zh: 各国政府面临越来越大的压力，必须实现具有法律约束力的净零目标，这要求从内燃机（ICE）车辆向电动汽车（EV）快速转型。设计有效的激励机制具有挑战性，因为车队调整缓慢、政策干预的财政成本高昂，并且电动化会侵蚀燃油税收入。本文构建了一个动态政策评估框架，将关于电动汽车采用的跨国证据与不确定性下的长期车队动态相结合。我们以英国和法国作为案例研究，模拟在替代政策目标下电动汽车购置激励的最优时间路径，这些目标包括终端车队目标、基于销量的惩罚以及财政收入考量。结果揭示了三个核心发现。第一，基于存量（终端）的惩罚可能会延迟干预，但会强烈稳定长期车队结果，而基于销量的惩罚则会诱发更早但针对性较弱的行动。第二，对燃油税收入的依赖会形成财政锁定机制，从而削弱最优电动化激励。第三，补贴项目的有效性关键取决于消费者对价格激励的响应程度。总体而言，分析表明，电动汽车转型政策最好与财政改革和长期车队动态结合起来评估。时机恰当且财政上协调一致的干预可以在限制长期预算风险的同时大幅减少排放。
title: Modeling optimal incentives for the electric vehicle market
title_zh: 电动汽车市场最优激励机制建模

abstract: The global cell phone market has transitioned significantly from feature phones to smartphones since 2007. This particular period of smartphone industry expansion, and a detailed product-level dataset of all the cell phones sold in 40 major economies between 2007 and 2016, give us an unprecedented chance to study how the order of entry affects the performance of the same firm in different markets. We begin with a theoretical framework wherein the order of a firm’s entry affects both consumers’ preferences and suppliers’ delivery costs. We then document a market sales advantage for early entrants, especially those originating from developed countries, offering higher-priced products, or having diversified product lines. Finally, we show that adopting product-specific innovations, such as the Android operating system and high-performance hardware components, can help late followers leapfrog over formerly leading firms.
abstract_zh: 自2007年以来，全球手机市场已从功能手机显著转向智能手机。智能手机产业这一特定扩张时期，以及2007年至2016年间40个主要经济体中所有已售手机的详细产品层面数据集，为我们研究进入顺序如何影响同一企业在不同市场中的表现提供了前所未有的机会。我们首先构建了一个理论框架，其中企业的进入顺序同时影响消费者偏好和供应商的交付成本。随后，我们记录了早期进入者的市场销售优势，尤其是那些来自发达国家、提供更高价格产品，或拥有多元化产品线的企业。最后，我们表明，采用针对特定产品的创新，如安卓操作系统和高性能硬件组件，可以帮助后期追随者超越此前的领先企业。
title: Order of Entry and Market Performance in the Global Smartphone Industry
title_zh: 全球智能手机行业的进入顺序与市场绩效

abstract: This paper examines the impact of changes in information and communication technologies (ICTs) on skilled and unskilled labor at the business cycle frequency. To achieve this, we construct aggregate hours series for both labor groups using the monthly outgoing rotation group of the Current Population Survey from 1994 to 2023. Our empirical analysis, conducted with a structural vector autoregressive model, shows that the working hours of both groups respond positively to ICT innovations with similar magnitudes. We demonstrate that our findings are consistent with a dynamic stochastic general equilibrium model in which ICT capital complements both skilled and unskilled labor, and suggest a plausible range of elasticity of substitution between capital and labor.
abstract_zh: 本文考察了信息与通信技术（ICT）变化在商业周期频率上对技能劳动力和非技能劳动力的影响。为实现这一目标，我们利用1994年至2023年当前人口调查的月度流出轮换组，构建了两个劳动力群体的总工时序列。我们使用结构向量自回归模型进行的实证分析表明，两个群体的工作时长对ICT创新均作出正向反应，且幅度相似。我们证明，我们的发现与一个动态随机一般均衡模型相一致，在该模型中，ICT资本与技能劳动力和非技能劳动力均互补，并提出资本与劳动力之间替代弹性的合理范围。
title: Information and communication technology innovations and labor hours: A business cycle analysis
title_zh: 信息通信技术创新与劳动时间：一个经济周期分析

abstract: In random-coefficient logit, compensating variation (CV) is a log-sum difference divided by the marginal utility of income. A log-sum-exp bound shows that pure price-change CV is bounded and has finite moments under every admissible coefficient distribution. For quality changes, finite moments of policy-relevant willingness-to-pay (WTP) coefficients are sufficient. Under independence, finite taste moments, and a nondegenerate policy effect, finite inverse moments of income sensitivity are also necessary. Mean welfare existence therefore depends on the policy and the induced coefficient distribution, not on preference- versus WTP-space parameterization itself. Simulations illustrate this distinction and show why finite sample means cannot establish the existence of a population mean.
abstract_zh: 在随机系数logit模型中，补偿变异（CV）是log-sum之差除以收入的边际效用。一个log-sum-exp界表明，在每一种可容许的系数分布下，纯价格变化的CV都是有界的且具有有限矩。对于质量变化，政策相关支付意愿（WTP）系数的有限矩是充分条件。在独立性、有限偏好矩以及非退化政策效应的条件下，收入敏感性的有限逆矩也是必要条件。因此，均值福利的存在性取决于政策及所诱导的系数分布，而不取决于偏好空间与WTP空间的参数化本身。模拟结果说明了这一区别，并表明为何有限样本均值无法确立总体均值的存在性。
title: When does the mean welfare change exist? Compensating variation and the price–quality divide in random-coefficient logit
title_zh: 平均福利变化何时存在？随机系数logit模型中的补偿变差与价格—质量二分

abstract: We show that bonds issued by financial firms have higher spreads than bonds issued by industrial firms with the same rating and maturity, a difference that we refer to as the financial premium. Over the period 1987 to 2020, in the United States, this premium is 43 basis points on average, with the premium higher for lower ratings, higher during financial crises, and increasing in bond beta. We derive a model that explains the financial premium: banks hold diversified portfolios of nonfinancial debt, and bank debt therefore reflects more systematic risk than nonfinancial debt.
abstract_zh: 我们发现，金融机构发行的债券相比同等评级和期限的工业企业的债券具有更高的利差，我们将这一差异称为金融溢价。在1987年至2020年间，美国的这一溢价平均为43个基点，且评级越低溢价越高，在金融危机期间溢价更高，并随着债券贝塔值的增加而增加。我们推导出一个模型来解释金融溢价：银行持有非金融债务的多样化投资组合，因此银行债务相比非金融债务反映了更多的系统性风险。
title: The Financial Premium

abstract: Women-owned-or-led small and medium-sized enterprises (WSMEs) are underrepresented in public and corporate supply chains worldwide. There is growing interest in promoting SMEs’ and WSMEs’ integration into value chains, but limited causal evidence whether interventions to support their participation in procurement are effective. This paper conducts a phased randomized controlled trial to estimate the impacts of corporate procurement training for WSMEs in Colombia. The program increases procurement knowledge and readiness, resulting in a ten percentage point increase in registrations to corporate portals, and an eight percentage point increase in the likelihood of submitting a bid. Impacts on winning bids are concentrated in WSMEs with prior procurement knowledge or experience, whose probability of winning a contract increases by eight to nine percentage points. These impacts are approximately twenty percent of the control means. More broadly, the paper illustrates how complier-weighted treatment effects can be used to evaluate programs delivered through a funnel-shaped participation process, common in private sector development interventions.
